Enter iosxe or ftd. Use iosxe for Cisco ISR-G2, ISR4K, or CSR routers.
Template presentation mode: basic or advanced. Basic omits parameters that have built-in recommended defaults.
FICTIONAL EXAMPLE ONLY. All addresses, identities and passwords are invented. Replace deployment values before use.
Enter the NETCONF management IPv4 address. Do not enter the WAN address.
Leave blank to reject name conflicts. Use replace_named only after reviewing an exact diff of the named objects.
Enter static or pbr. Recommendation: use pbr when selected source LANs must reach 0.0.0.0/0 through Secure Access.
Enter the current ISP next-hop IPv4 address. Recommendation: copy it from the verified active default route.
Enter the router WAN IPv4 address used by the IKEv2 policy local-address match. It can be private when the ISR is behind NAT.
IOS XE object-name prefix. Recommended value: sse; use another short unique prefix only when required.
IKEv2 encryption. Cisco recommends GCM for maximum throughput; recommended value: aes-gcm-256.
IKEv2 pseudo-random function. SHA256 is required with the recommended AES-GCM proposal.
IKEv2 integrity algorithm. Leave blank with AES-GCM because GCM provides authenticated encryption; use the portal-approved hash with CBC.
IKEv2 Diffie-Hellman groups separated by |. Recommended ISR proposal: 19|20; Secure Access also supports 14 and 15.
IPsec ESP transform. Cisco recommends GCM for throughput; recommended value: esp-gcm-256.
Optional IPsec PFS group. Recommendation: leave blank unless required and tested; Cisco warns PFS preference can cause rekey failures.
IKE rekey interval in seconds. Recommended Secure Access default: 14400 seconds (4 hours).
Child SA/IPsec rekey interval in seconds. Recommended Secure Access default: 3600 seconds (1 hour).
DPD interval in seconds. The Cisco ISR example uses 10 seconds; use 30 seconds when intentionally matching the Secure Access 156-second maximum timeout design.
DPD retry value used by the ISR profile. Recommended ISR guide value: 3; verify the resulting failover timing in production testing.
Test build only. Enter the NETCONF username.
Test build only. Enter the NETCONF password. It is redacted from all generated output.
Enter a management network in CIDR notation, for example 198.51.100.0/24. Recommendation: bypass it from PBR to preserve router access.
Enter a Secure Access destination in CIDR notation. Use 0.0.0.0/0 to steer all destinations selected by the PBR source ACL.
Enter one PBR source LAN in CIDR notation; copy this row with a unique item number for each LAN. Include only networks intended for Secure Access.
Optional. Enter a destination that must use normal routing. Leave every bypass row blank to generate only source-to-destination permit entries.
Enter the IOS XE LAN interface where matching traffic arrives, for example GigabitEthernet0/0/1. Cisco requires the route-map on the ingress interface.
Enter normal-routing. This returns traffic to the normal RIB/ISP when no PBR set action is usable; verify this behavior during failover testing.
Enter TunnelN, for example Tunnel2. Recommendation: choose an unused ID from the fresh router inventory.
Enter create for an unused interface or reuse for an existing interface. Reuse requires a reviewed current-versus-proposed diff.
Enter the Secure Access data-center IPv4 address shown in the tunnel group. Recommendation: use the closest assigned data center.
Enter the Tunnel ID/email from the Secure Access portal.

Enter an existing interface whose IPv4 address the VTI will borrow. Cisco ISR examples use ip unnumbered; use either this field or address.
Enter a CIDR address only when the plan must create a new loopback used as the tunnel source; otherwise leave blank.
